newsitem.title: ITALY: Political party headed by Italy's Dini splits up.
newsitem.headline: Political party headed by Italy's Dini splits up.

text.p: Italian Renewal, a small centrist party which backs the government and is headed by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, has split up in parliament after months of infighting.
A group of 11 parliamentarians from the lower house decided to break away from Italian Renewal late on Saturday, leaving Dini's party with just 14 members in the 630-seat Chamber of Deputies.

The batch of defectors will join the so-called Mixed Group of smaller parties but pledged to carry on backing Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left coalition, which falls short of a majority in the Chamber and has to rely on the hardline Communist Refoundation for survival.

Under Italian law, no party can operate independently in the lower house if it has less than 20 deputies, meaning that the group of politicians remaining faithful to Dini will also have to join the mixed benches.

"Our group is therefore dissolved," said Diego Masi, the parliamentary party leader of Italian Renewal, who led the break-away from Dini. "However we will remain faithful to the coalition government and loyal to Prodi," he added.
Italian Renewal was created earlier this year ahead of the April general election and sucked in various groups from the splintered centre of Italian politics.
However tensions rapidly developed, with some party members accusing Dini of using the group purely for his own benefit and ignoring calls for a change of political strategy.
Factions within the group have refused to stand together at forthcoming regional elections and have failed to agree on a joint stance in talks over constitutional reform.

Dini did not attend Saturday's meeting and made no comment on the split. Political sources said Italian Renewal's 11-strong team in the Senate (upper house) would also split up at a meeting scheduled for next week.
